title: Medical Administrative & Surgical Patient Coordinator | Mexico
description:
About Us
HireHawk connects skilled professionals around the world with meaningful remote opportunities supporting U.S. and Canadian companies. We focus on long-term placements where experienced professionals can take real ownership, become trusted members of the team, and make a measurable impact from anywhere.
About the Role
As a Medical Administrative & Surgical Patient Coordinator, you will own the administrative coordination that happens after a patient begins moving through the surgical process. You will make sure required clearances, testing, records, appointments, documentation, and pre-operative steps are completed so patients stay on track for surgery.
This is an operations-focused healthcare role, not a sales position and not a remote clinical position. You will work directly with patients, medical offices, imaging centers, laboratories, hospitals, and other healthcare providers while knowing when a question or concern needs to be escalated to clinical staff. You will receive training on the practice's specific workflows and gradually take ownership of a critical part of the patient journey.
Responsibilities

• Own and track the pre-operative process for multiple surgical patients from booking through readiness for surgery.

• Keep each patient's pre-operative checklist current, identifying missing clearances, tests, records, documentation, and other requirements before they become delays.

• Coordinate required appointments and testing, including imaging, medical clearances, laboratory work, and other pre-operative requirements.

• Contact hospitals, imaging centers, laboratories, physicians' offices, and other healthcare facilities to obtain outstanding information and keep cases moving.

• Follow up persistently with outside providers when testing, records, or clearances are delayed, advocating for patients while maintaining professional communication.

• Conduct or support standardized pre-operative patient calls and clearly walk patients through established non-clinical instructions and next steps.

• Maintain accurate documentation of patient conversations, completed requirements, pending items, and case status within the appropriate systems.

• Communicate surgical readiness, outstanding requirements, and potential delays clearly to the broader practice team.

• Recognize clinical questions, unusual circumstances, or concerns that fall outside your administrative scope and escalate them promptly rather than providing independent medical advice.

• Provide additional medical administrative and patient-coordination support when needed to improve the efficiency of the surgical process.

Requirements

Must-Have:

• 3+ years of experience in medical administration, surgical coordination, patient coordination, pre-operative coordination, or closely related healthcare operations.

• Hands-on experience working in a U.S. medical practice or healthcare environment.

• Direct experience coordinating surgical or pre-operative patients, including appointments, tests, medical records, clearances, or required documentation.

• Experience using EMR, CRM, patient-management, or comparable medical-office systems.

• Confidence communicating directly with patients and contacting hospitals, imaging centers, laboratories, physicians' offices, and other healthcare providers.

• Excellent spoken and written English, with strong documentation, organization, case-tracking, and follow-through skills.

• Sound judgment regarding administrative versus clinical responsibilities, including knowing when an issue must be escalated to clinical staff.

Nice to Have:

• Experience in plastic surgery, cosmetic surgery, aesthetics, or another high-touch private-pay medical environment.

• Medical Assistant training, nursing-related education, healthcare education, or equivalent clinical-office experience.

• Experience conducting standardized pre-operative patient calls.

OUR MISSION:

At Sunrise Robotics, we are dedicated to augmenting humanity through intelligent robotics. Our mission is to elevate the world of manufacturing by introducing intelligent, flexible robots that enhance human capabilities and existing machinery, ushering in the next era of production at higher quality, with less waste, and lower cost.

OUR VISION:

We see a future where every element of manufacturing, from design to assembly, is optimised with intelligent automation. Our vision is to integrate flexible robotic solutions, based on generic hardware and advanced software/AI capabilities, into manufacturing, particularly in small and medium-sized enterprises, to make automation economically viable and accessible, for all sizes of manufacturers. We are not just building robots; we are creating the strategically crucial components for autonomous, intelligent agents of the future.

THE ROLE

At Sunrise Robotics, this role owns the safety of our robotic cells as a product, from the first design decision to the cell running on a customer's floor. That covers functional safety, safety in our robotics software, and the sign-off of every deployment.

Our robotic cells combine two industrial robot arms, cameras, a safety PLC, radar presence sensing and software that changes what the cell does from one product variant to the next. Every new application changes the hazards. Your job is to know exactly what changed, and to stop us repeating safety work for everything that didn't.

You are part of the design, not a check at the end. You work with our robotics and software engineers on motion planning, perception and how the cell behaves around people, and decide early which risks need a safety function and which the software can handle.

We are creating a new way of doing high-mix manufacturing, and safety standards were written for machines that do one fixed job. That leaves a grey zone where the standards give no clean answer. We need someone creative who can operate in that grey zone and bring clarity: work out a safe answer, defend it, and write it down so others can follow it. That means being creative about how we reach a safe design, never about whether a design is safe.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

- The safety concept for our cell platform: which hazards and safety functions are assessed once, so each new application assesses only what it changes.

- Safety in design: input to our robotics software from the first design review, safety requirements in every product and application requirements document, and sign-off on each solution design.

- Functional safety: you specify each safety function in the safety PLC and robot safety controller, including how reliable it must be, and prove it works. Our robotics integration engineer writes the PLC code.

- Risk assessments, the CE technical file and the Declaration of Conformity for each cell, including our move to the new EU Machinery Regulation.

- Site safety for each deployment, from layout and guarding to operator access, and safety checks at every acceptance test.

- Our rules for testing cells safely in R&D, including Reduced Safety Mode.

- Root cause investigation of safety faults and incidents.

- Safety content for the cell manual, and customers' safety questions in presales.

- At least five years of machinery safety work on industrial machines or robotic cells, including risk assessments and CE marking you prepared or signed.

- Functional safety experience: specifying and validating safety functions on safety PLCs, robot safety controllers and safety sensors such as radar, scanners and light curtains.

- Working knowledge of EU machinery law, including the new Machinery Regulation, and of the two core standards: ISO 12100 for risk assessment and ISO 13849 for functional safety.
